stem: Which is income earned from owning shares in a company?

options.content: Dividend
options.rationale: Correct: a share of the company's profit paid to shareholders.

options.content: Rent
options.rationale: Rent is earned from land and buildings.

options.content: Wages
options.rationale: Wages are earned from labour.

options.content: Commission
options.rationale: Commission is paid to agents and salespeople.

explanation: Shareholders receive dividends out of the company's profit.

options.content: Money borrowed from a bank to buy goods
options.rationale: That is borrowing, not saving.

options.content: Spending on goods that last a long time
options.rationale: Durable goods are still consumption spending.

options.content: Income that is not spent on consumption now
options.rationale: Correct: saving = income − consumption spending.

options.content: Paying tax to the government
options.rationale: Tax is a deduction from income, not saving.

explanation: Saving is the part of income kept for future use rather than spent now.

stem: Which method of saving earns no interest and carries the greatest risk of theft?

options.content: A savings account at a bank
options.rationale: Bank savings earn interest and are kept safely.

options.content: A fixed deposit
options.rationale: A fixed deposit earns a higher interest rate.

options.content: A post office savings account
options.rationale: This earns interest and is held by an institution.

options.content: Keeping cash at home
options.rationale: Correct: no interest and it can be stolen or lost.

explanation: Cash at home is easy to reach but earns nothing and is exposed to theft and fire.

stem: Why does a fixed deposit usually pay a higher interest rate than an ordinary savings account?

options.content: Fixed deposits are free from all risk
options.rationale: No investment is entirely free from risk.

options.content: The saver can withdraw at any time
options.rationale: Early withdrawal is restricted on a fixed deposit.

options.content: The government pays part of the interest
options.rationale: Banks pay the interest, not the government.

options.content: The money is left for an agreed period
options.rationale: Correct: the bank can lend it out for longer with certainty.

explanation: Savers accept that the money is tied up for a fixed time, and are rewarded with a higher rate.

stem: Which of these is a personal **investment** rather than saving?

options.content: Putting part of a salary into a money box
options.rationale: That is saving: no income-earning asset is bought.

options.content: Buying a small flat to rent out
options.rationale: Correct: an asset bought to earn rent and grow in value.

options.content: Not spending a bonus this month
options.rationale: Not spending is saving.

options.content: Paying a monthly bill for electricity
options.rationale: That is consumption spending.

explanation: Investment uses savings to buy an asset that is expected to earn income or rise in value.

stem: A young worker wants money available at short notice for emergencies. Which is the most suitable place for these savings?

options.content: Shares in a listed company
options.rationale: Share prices may be low just when the money is needed.

options.content: A plot of land
options.rationale: Land is slow to sell and costly to buy.

options.content: A bank savings account
options.rationale: Correct: safe, earns some interest and can be withdrawn quickly.

options.content: A five-year fixed deposit
options.rationale: The money is tied up for five years.

explanation: Emergency savings need liquidity and safety more than a high return.
hints: Which option can be turned into cash fastest without losing value?

stem: Which statement best explains why a family might invest in livestock?

options.content: Livestock carry no risk of loss
options.rationale: Disease, drought and theft are real risks.

options.content: Animals can multiply and may keep value when prices rise
options.rationale: Correct: offspring add value and livestock may hold value in inflation.

options.content: Livestock pay a fixed rate of interest
options.rationale: Interest is paid on deposits and loans, not on animals.

options.content: Livestock can be sold instantly at a known price
options.rationale: Prices vary and buyers must be found.

explanation: Livestock produce offspring, milk or eggs and can hold value, but they carry risks.
hints: Think about how cattle or goats increase in number.

stem: Thandeka saves US\$750 in an account that pays simple interest. Assume a rate of 8% a year. Calculate the total interest she earns in 3 years.

Sipho buys shares for US\$1,600. During the year he receives a dividend of US\$64, and at the end of the year the shares are worth US\$1,720. Calculate his total return as a percentage of the amount invested, to one decimal place.
hints: Include both the dividend and the rise in value.

stem: Rudo's monthly income is US\$540 and she spends US\$465 on consumption. How much does she save each month?
A person must have savings before making a personal investment.
explanation: True. Investment uses savings (or borrowed money) to buy an income-earning asset; saving comes first.

stem: Shares always pay a fixed dividend every year.
explanation: False. Ordinary share dividends depend on profits and the directors' decision; they can be cut or not paid.

stem: Match each source of personal income with the person who earns it.

right.content: A saver with a fixed deposit
A vendor who sells vegetables at a market stall
A factory worker paid for hours worked
A landlord who lets out a shop

explanation: Each factor of production earns its own type of income.

payload.template: Saving aims mainly at {{blank:a}} and quick access to the money. Investment aims mainly at a higher {{blank:b}}, but carries more risk.

explanation: Savings are kept safe and liquid; investments seek a return at higher risk.

stem: Name the type of bank account in which money is left for an agreed period at a higher rate of interest.
explanation: A fixed (time) deposit ties money up for an agreed period in return for higher interest.

points.description: Reason, e.g. emergencies such as illness or loss of a job (1)
Explained: savings avoid borrowing at high cost when money is needed suddenly (1)
Reason, e.g. future purchases / retirement / starting a business / earn interest (1)
Explained, e.g. school fees or a business needs a large sum that monthly income cannot cover (1)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: People save for emergencies such as illness, so that they do not have to borrow at a high cost. They also save for large future spending such as school fees or starting a business, which cannot be paid from one month's income.

explanation: Each reason must be stated and developed.
hints: Think about the unexpected and the planned.

stem: Explain **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of a savings club (rotating savings group) compared with a bank savings account.

points.description: Advantage, e.g. encourages discipline / no bank charges / lump sum available sooner (1)
Explained, e.g. members receive the full pool to buy stock in bulk (1)
Disadvantage, e.g. no interest / risk that a member defaults or the money is stolen (1)
Explained, e.g. no legal protection, so members may lose their contributions (1)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A savings club makes members save every month and gives each member a large lump sum in turn, which can buy stock in bulk. However, it pays no interest and has no legal protection, so if a member stops paying the others may lose money.

explanation: Savings clubs give discipline and lump sums but carry risk and earn no interest.
hints: Who guarantees the money in each case?

stem: Tendai, aged 58, has saved US\$2,500 and plans to retire in two years. A bank offers a one-year fixed deposit; assume an interest rate of 7% a year. A friend suggests buying shares instead, which he expects to pay a dividend of US\$90 and to be worth US\$2,650 after one year.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the interest Tendai would earn on the fixed deposit in one year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total expected return from the shares in one year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State **two** risks of investing in shares.

points.description: Share price may fall (1)
Dividend may be cut or not paid / company may fail (1)

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Recommend whether Tendai should choose the fixed deposit or the shares. Justify your answer.

points.description: Shares expected to earn more (US\$240 against US\$175) (1)
But the share return is only expected; fixed deposit interest is agreed (1)
Tendai retires soon and needs his money safe / cannot wait for prices to recover (1)
Justified recommendation (1)

explanation: Fixed deposit US\$175; shares expected US\$240. With retirement close, safety matters more than a higher but uncertain return.
hints: Return on shares = dividend + rise in value.

stem: Chipo, a teacher in Gweru, receives a monthly salary. She also rents out a room in her house and owns some shares. She keeps her spare cash in a tin at home.

points.description: Salary (1)
Rent (1)
Dividends (1)
Saving: income not spent, kept for later use (1)
Investment: using savings to buy an asset that earns income or grows in value (1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why Chipo should move her spare cash from the tin to a bank savings account.

points.description: Earns interest (1)
Safe from theft or fire (1)
Value better protected from inflation / still available when needed (1)

explanation: Chipo earns a salary, rent and dividends. Saving keeps money for later; investment buys income-earning assets. A bank account is safer and earns interest.
hints: Each asset she owns gives a different type of income.
